harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured logrotate on node1 (Alpine) to rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily, keep 7 compressed rotations, and let the app keep writing after rotation via copytruncate. Installed logrotate, wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app, wired it into the existing crond daily periodic job (and started/enabled crond, which was previously stopped and not in the default runlevel), and verified functionally before and after a full node restart.
actions_performed: Investigated node1 baseline: Alpine 3.23, app.log existed with static content, no logrotate installed, no logrotate.d entry for it, crond binary present but service stopped/not enabled
Installed logrotate package via apk
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app: daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate, create 0644 root root
Enabled and started the crond service (rc-update add crond default; rc-service crond start) so the existing /etc/periodic/daily -> run-parts wiring will actually fire logrotate
Dry-ran (logrotate -d) and force-ran (logrotate -vf) the config twice to prove immediate gzip compression and correct .1.gz->.2.gz chaining up to the 7-rotation retention
Verified app.log remains writable immediately after copytruncate-based rotation (no restart/signal needed for the writer)
Cleaned up test rotation artifacts and restored app.log to its original baseline content/perms
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline for node1
Rebooted node1 via sudo -n reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec was available again

Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, confirmed crond still running and enabled, confirmed logrotate config persisted, re-ran a forced rotation and a post-rotation write to confirm functionality survived the restart, then restored app.log to baseline again

evidence.requirement: Baseline investigation: no rotation configured, app.log location/content, crond/logrotate absent
evidence.summary: Showed Alpine OS, app.log with 60 bytes of content, no logrotate installed, no logrotate.d entry, crond present but not yet examined

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation, 7 compressed rotations, continued writability configured and functionally verified
evidence.summary: Installed logrotate, wrote daily/rotate 7/compress/copytruncate config, dry-run validated it, then forced two rotations proving immediate .gz compression and correct chain (.1.gz -> .2.gz), and proved app.log accepted new writes right after rotation via copytruncate

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation actually scheduled to run (not just configured)
evidence.summary: Found crond was stopped and not in the default runlevel; enabled it with rc-update add crond default and started it, confirmed status started and crond listed under default runlevel, so the existing 0 2 * * * run-parts /etc/periodic/daily cron entry will invoke logrotate

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id fc3ba3a3-bef5-4561-b9b7-9595c50ea90c, confirmed crond started, logrotate config valid via dry-run, and app.log present with expected content

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement, disconnect, and reconnection
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded sudo -n reboot so the ack returned before disconnect; subsequent probes failed (connection reset, then timed out) proving the node went down; a later probe succeeded proving reconnection

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity and post-restart recovery of logrotate config, crond, and app.log/rotation functionality
evidence.summary: New boot_id 637f4790-82ac-4cfa-8a98-332cf3a85a3c differs from baseline fc3ba3a3..., crond still started and enabled in default runlevel, logrotate.d config intact, and a fresh forced rotation plus post-rotation write succeeded, confirming full functional recovery after restart; app.log was then restored to its original baseline content
